name: Volume Serial Number (VSN)
location: SOFTWARE\Microsoft\WindowsNT\CurrentVersion\EMDMgmt - find the key matching the device's Volume Name and USB Unique Serial Number, then take the last integer in the matching line and convert it from decimal to hex to get the VSN; this key is often missing entirely on modern systems using SSD-based removable devices. Windows 10+: Microsoft-Windows-Partition/Diagnostic.evtx Event ID 1006 may include VBR data containing the VSN - 4 bytes located at offset 0x43 (FAT), 0x64 (exFAT), or 0x48 (NTFS) within each Volume Boot Record; this log is cleared during major OS feature updates.
purpose: Discovers the Volume Serial Number assigned to the file-system partition on a USB device - this is NOT the USB Unique Serial Number hardcoded into the device's firmware, nor any external label serial number - for correlating the device to files or shell items it produced elsewhere on the system.
key_fields: EMDMgmt key/value name - encodes the device's Volume Name and USB Unique Serial Number together with a trailing decimal integer that is the VSN once converted to hex
Partition/Diagnostic.evtx Event ID 1006 VBR payload - fixed-offset 4-byte VSN field, offset depends on the partition's file system (FAT 0x43, exFAT 0x64, NTFS 0x48)
normal_baseline: A consistent VSN recoverable across all available sources (EMDMgmt, VBR data in Event ID 1006, and any shell-item metadata in LNK files/shellbags/jump lists) for the same physical device over its lifetime on the system.
anomalies: A VSN recovered from shell-item metadata (LNK, shellbags, jump lists) with no matching EMDMgmt entry - on modern/SSD-based devices this can simply reflect the key's frequent absence rather than tampering, so weigh it alongside other USB artifacts before treating it as suspicious

Two connection events attributed to what is claimed to be the same physical device yielding different VSNs, consistent with the device having been reformatted or with two different devices being presented as one

A device's VSN appearing in LNK/shellbags shell-item data on a host with no corresponding usb-device-history or usb-event-logs record for that device, suggesting deleted or missing upstream USB artifacts
Partition/Diagnostic.evtx showing a gap spanning a known device-connection window, consistent with the log having been reset by a major OS feature update rather than by user action
anti_forensic_notes: EMDMgmt is frequently absent entirely on modern systems and SSD-based removable media, so its absence alone carries little weight; the Partition/Diagnostic.evtx channel is cleared during major Windows feature updates, meaning a VSN capture opportunity from that source can be lost across an OS-upgrade boundary independent of any deliberate anti-forensic action.
interpretation: The VSN is not the USB Unique Serial Number hardcoded into the device's firmware, nor any printed external label serial - it belongs to the file-system partition and changes if the device is reformatted. The VSN together with the device's Volume Name is what allows correlation of a specific USB device to files it touched elsewhere on the system, via shell items embedded in LNK files and other registry locations such as shellbags.
